newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates rise after sudden fall.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates rise after sudden fall.

text.p: Dutch call money rates jumped back to a level above the special advances rate on Wednesday, after dipping as low as 2.00 percent bid yesterday.
The bid price of overnight money was around 2.50-2.62 percent late on Wednesday afternoon and dealers said the price had been higher during the session.
"Call money remains volatile as the inflow and outflow of liquidity differs greatly from day to day," said one dealer.
Dealers said the Dutch central bank was most certainly leaving the special advances rate at 2.50 percent when it sets a new pact at 1400 GMT.
Market players said the decision by the Fed to leave the discount rate unchanged had no effect on the money market.
Three-month deposits were unchanged at 2.70 percent bid in thin trade.
The guilder was virtually unchanged against the mark at 112.13 per 100 marks from 112.135 on Tuesday.
